version.changelog:
No code changes in this version; documentation updates only.

- Clarified data retention: detection request payloads are not persisted, while account data is stored for billing and account management.
- Updated description of local credentials storage, noting use of plaintext JSON to match common CLI tools.
- Minor edits to improve accuracy and detail regarding transmission and retention of agent metadata.

llm.summary: The skill's documentation and stated behavior are generally coherent for a local-first security plugin, but there are a few unexplained/inconsistent claims and unverifiable assertions (no code included in the skill bundle), so you should audit the upstream project and registration flow before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, and instructions all describe a runtime security plugin that hooks into tool events. The declared lack of required binaries/env/config is consistent with an instruction-only guide that points to an external repository and npm package for the actual plugin code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md is documentation-only and does not itself run code, which keeps the skill surface small. It instructs the operator to install a plugin that will hook into before_tool_call/after_tool_call/tool_result_persist — i.e., the plugin (if installed) would see all tool calls and parameters. The doc promises local-only protections and sanitization, but those guarantees are unverifiable from the instruction file alone and the doc describes an activation/registration step that will return and store an API key locally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are included in the skill bundle (instruction-only). That minimizes immediate disk execution risk in this package, but the doc points you to external sources (GitHub, npm). Real risk depends on which upstream package you actually install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md declares no required env vars or credentials for the skill itself. It does describe an opt-in registration that returns an API key and agent ID stored locally; the doc also says account data (agent ID, email, plan tier) is stored on the service for billing — the text is slightly inconsistent (registration claims to send only {name, description}, yet the doc later mentions storing email), so verify what information the upstream service actually collects before registering. Storing an API key locally is expected but is a sensitive operation worth auditing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: This skill is not flagged always:true and is user-invocable. However, the plugin it documents is intended to hook into core agent events (giving it broad visibility into all tool calls). That level of access is expected for a guardrail plugin, but it means you should only install the upstream code if you trust and/or have audited it.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This SKILL.md is documentation-only and does not itself execute, but it points to an upstream open-source plugin that would need to be installed to get these protections. Before installing or registering: 1) Audit the upstream repository (especially files called out: sanitizer.ts, content-injection-scanner.ts, index.ts) and confirm the npm package name and contents match the repo. 2) Verify exactly what data the registration call sends and what the service stores (the doc has a minor inconsistency about email collection). 3) Prefer local-only mode if you need strong privacy guarantees; confirm via code review that 'local-only' truly avoids sending raw content. 4) Treat any API key returned as sensitive and inspect how/where it is stored. 5) If you cannot audit the upstream package, consider not installing a plugin that will receive all tool calls and parameters.
